decisions_made: IWorldHist gained an additional clause (H1-acc): '∀ c', parAncestor par c' c → isAccessible edges c' c = true', beyond the report's literal (H1)-(H5), because (H1) alone (bare edge membership) cannot supply Phase 7's mint-arm need for genuine multi-hop isAccessible facts about arbitrary-distance ancestors without re-deriving them from a fixed edges snapshot -- which Phase 1 already showed has a provable one-unit fuel deficit. This is additive; none of (H1)-(H5) were removed or weakened.

The plan's Phase 6 task list ('thread both companions through the key induction's hypothesis list') was NOT executed literally, because this same phase's own Exit Criteria explicitly prohibits asserting the invariant as an established conclusion of the induction before the arms are proved, and explicitly sanctions deferring the induction wiring to Phases 7-8 when intermediate scaffolding is unavoidable. All pieces were delivered as complete, sorry-free, standalone declarations instead; intExpandBranches_openBranch_sat's signature and key statement are unchanged by this phase.

Phase 3's hNC hypothesis remains linter-flagged as unreferenced by design, not neglect: its sole planned consumer (intFImp_mint_residue's hNC parameter) is reachable only from inside the mint arm, which this phase's Exit Criteria forbids touching. Fabricating an artificial use to silence the linter was rejected as gaming the warning rather than addressing it.

parAncestor was defined via Relation.ReflTransGen (fun a b => a = par b), matching the file's existing intAccessPreorder style (also built on Relation.ReflTransGen), rather than a hand-rolled inductive relation.

IWorldHist's second explicit parameter (the expanded-set list e, present for signature parity with the file's other 4-list-zip companions) is named _e (not e) to silence the unusedVariables linter, since IWorldHist's own clauses do not reference it -- matching the report's own draft signature, which likewise never uses e in the body.
